# Part 1: Get to know your pitcher

This part is for you. It won't go in the report, but you can't build the report without it.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

trackman <- read_csv("data/raw/trackman_fall_2026.csv")
```

We're using the same colors for every pitcher, so that a slider is the same color in every report coach gets. Run this as is. If your pitcher throws a pitch type that isn't here, add it.

```{r}
#| echo: false

okabe_ito <- unname(palette.colors(palette = "Okabe-Ito")[2:8])

pitch_colors <- c(
  "Fastball" = okabe_ito[1],
  "FourSeamFastBall" = okabe_ito[1],
  "Sinker" = okabe_ito[4],
  "ChangeUp" = okabe_ito[5],
  "Splitter" = okabe_ito[2],
  "Slider" = okabe_ito[3],
  "Sweeper" = okabe_ito[6],
  "Curveball" = okabe_ito[7],
  "Cutter" = "black",
  "Undefined" = "gray50"
)
```

> Filter to your pitcher. How many pitches does he have, and over how many days? Which hand does he throw with?

```{r}
#| echo: false
gonzalez <- trackman |>
  filter(Pitcher == "Gonzalez, Giancarlo") |>
  mutate(HorzBreak = -HorzBreak)

gonzalez |>
  summarise(pitches = n(), days = n_distinct(Date), throwing_hand = first(PitcherThrows))
```

> Compare `TaggedPitchType` and `AutoPitchType` for your pitcher. Which column will you use, and why? I will use taggedpitchtype, the trackman is not great at discerning pitch types from d3 pitchers and I doubt a d3 pitcher is throwing so many different types of pitches.

```{r}
#| echo: false
gonzalez |> 
  count(TaggedPitchType, AutoPitchType)
```

> Which pitch types does he throw often enough to say something about? What will you do with the rest? Changup, fastball, sinker, and slider. I will leave out cutter because 3 is not enough pitches to go off of.

**If your pitcher throws left-handed:** horizontal break is backwards for him compared to Hale To fix it, flip the sign of HorzBreak when you filter to your pitcher so that positive means "arm side" for every pitcher. To do this you would include `mutate(HorzBreak = -HorzBreak`. This is only necessary if your pitcher is left handed.

```{r}
#| echo: false

gonzalez_main <- gonzalez |>
  filter(TaggedPitchType %in% c("Fastball", "Slider", "ChangeUp", "Sinker"))

movement_summary <- gonzalez_main |>
  group_by(TaggedPitchType) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    RelSpeed = mean(RelSpeed, na.rm = TRUE),
    horizontal = mean(HorzBreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    vertical = mean(InducedVertBreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(TaggedPitchType, " (n=", n, ")"),
    label_x = case_when(
      TaggedPitchType == "Fastball" ~ horizontal + 2,
      TaggedPitchType == "Sinker" ~ horizontal + 2,
      TaggedPitchType == "ChangeUp" ~ horizontal + 2,
      TRUE ~ horizontal + 2
    ),
    label_y = case_when(
      TaggedPitchType == "Fastball" ~ vertical - 2,
      TaggedPitchType == "Sinker" ~ vertical + 2,
      TRUE ~ vertical
    )
  )

release_summary <- gonzalez_main |>
  group_by(TaggedPitchType) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    side = mean(RelSide, na.rm = TRUE) * 12,
    height = mean(RelHeight, na.rm = TRUE) * 12,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(TaggedPitchType, " (n=", n, ")"),
    label_x = case_when(
      TaggedPitchType == "Fastball" ~ side + 1,
      TaggedPitchType == "Sinker" ~ side - 1,
      TaggedPitchType == "Slider" ~ side - 1,
      TRUE ~ side + 1
    ),
    label_y = case_when(
      TaggedPitchType == "Fastball" ~ height + 1,
      TaggedPitchType == "Sinker" ~ height - 1,
      TaggedPitchType == "Slider" ~ height + 1,
      TRUE ~ height - 1
    )
  )
```

# Part 2: The report

Everything in this part goes to coach.

## His movement profile

> Make a movement profile for your pitcher that coach can read without you in the room. Use what we did in class: labels instead of a legend, how many pitches are behind each label, the raw pitches in the background, and a title that tells coach what to see.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
gonzalez_main |>
  ggplot(aes(x = HorzBreak, y = InducedVertBreak,
             color = TaggedPitchType, shape = TaggedPitchType)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pitch_colors) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_label(data = movement_summary,
             aes(x = horizontal, y = vertical, label = label),
             color = "black") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Gonzalez's slider breaks opposite his fastball and sinker",
    x = "Horizontal break (inches; positive = arm side)",
    y = "Induced vertical break (inches)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## His release geometry

`RelSide` and `RelHeight` are where the ball leaves his hand, in feet: side to side, and how high. (Check the glossary for where 0 is.) Coaches care about this because if one pitch comes out of a different spot than the others, a hitter can pick it up early.

> Make a figure that answers: **does every pitch come out of the same place?** The design is up to you. A few things to think about:
>
> - Both axes are in feet. What did Wilke say about that?
> - The differences here might be small. Is a foot the right unit for coach?
> - Does coach need every pitch, the average for each pitch type, or both?
> - Each pitch type has to be the same color it was in your movement profile.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
gonzalez_main |>
  ggplot(aes(x = RelSide * 12, y = RelHeight * 12,
             color = TaggedPitchType, shape = TaggedPitchType)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pitch_colors) +
  geom_label(data = release_summary,
             aes(x = side, y = height, label = label),
             color = "black", show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Gonzalez releases his changeup lower than his fastball",
    subtitle = "The average fastball release is about 5 inches higher than the changeup",
    x = "Release side (inches)",
    y = "Release height (inches above ground)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## A note for coach

> In **150 words or fewer**, tell coach what to look at in each figure and what it means for this pitcher. Include one thing he should be careful about (for example, how many pitches something is based on, or which pitch type column you used).
>
> Gonzalez's fastball and sinker both move toward his arm side, while his slider breaks in the opposite direction. His changeup has less arm-side movement than either fastball or sinker. The large dots show each pitch's average movement, and the smaller dots show how much individual pitches vary. In the release chart, the fastball tends to come out higher and closer to the center of the field than the other pitches. His changeup has a noticeably lower average release point, which could give hitters an early clue about what is coming. Both figures use the tagged pitch types, since the automatic classifications often disagree. Also, the sinker has only 15 observations, so its average is less certain than the fastball, slider, or changeup averages.

# Part 3: Behind the report

This part is for me, not coach.

> Was there anything in the data you weren't sure about for your pitcher? What did you do about it?
>
> The automatic pitch classifications did not always match the tagged classifications, so I compared the two columns, used TaggedPitchType for both figures, and excluded the cutter because it had only three pitches. I also reversed the horizontal break for this left-handed pitcher so that positive values mean arm-side movement.
